key_insight: An LLM’s readable reasoning is not necessarily a faithful account of its internal computations. Monitoring that text alone may therefore provide an incomplete picture of how the model reaches its answers.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of understanding and monitoring reasoning LLMs when their step-by-step explanations do not accurately reflect their underlying computations.
method: Examines the distinction between human-readable reasoning tokens and internal model computations.
Highlights the implications of this mismatch for monitoring reasoning LLMs.
The supplied abstract does not specify experiments, datasets, or a concrete monitoring method.
impact: AI/ML practitioners should not treat readable reasoning as a guaranteed explanation of model behavior. Reliable oversight requires evaluating what reasoning-text monitoring can—and cannot—reveal.
visual_elements: Split-view diagram contrasting visible reasoning text with hidden internal computations.
Flowchart showing a prompt, internal processing, reasoning text, and final answer, with uncertain links marked.
Magnifying-glass icon over reasoning text to illustrate the limited scope of text-based monitoring.
paper_title: Towards understanding and monitorability of reasoning LLMs
